notes: Labeled identity pairs for gp-cami. `truth` lists ground-truth clusters: every ref in a cluster is the same real person. The ssn-* records exist to measure what plan 2 (SSN removal) costs — when the tier goes, they become a false split and the recall floor must be re-baselined, not lowered silently. The ssn-* hash is a synthetic sha512 of the literal string gp-cami-eval-fixture-synthetic-ssn-grace-adeyemi, so it is reproducible, deliberately NOT a filler value — filler SSNs are what SsnHashGuard blocks, and merging on one would be a defect, not a true positive. The nodob-a/nodob-b pair (same name, no DOB on either record) is kept apart in `truth` as a deliberate POLICY assertion — never merge on name alone without a DOB, no matter how suggestive the name match looks — not a conclusion drawn from the available evidence, so nobody should later 'correct' the answer key to merge them. smith-other's and chain-a's NPIs were originally 1987654327 / 1112223339, which are NOT Luhn-valid under the 80840-prefixed NPI check digit despite looking like plausible 10-digit NPIs — corrected to 1987654328 / 1112223338 (same 9 leading digits, recomputed check digit) once NPI validation was added in plan 5. See EvalFixtureNpiValidityTest, which pins this. The mmis-* and dea-* records were added by plan 5 to exercise the two match keys it promotes, and each merge pair is deliberately paired with a foil in the fixture pattern already set by smith-other/garcia-other/kowalski-other: mmis-other-state carries the SAME MMIS number in a different state and must never merge (MMIS numbers are per-state Medicaid identifiers, so the same digits in CA and TX are two different registrations), and dea-other shares the name but carries a different DEA number. Without those two foils the gate would prove the new tiers can merge and prove nothing about whether they over-merge. DEA rows carry no state at all because DEA registration is federal.
